exercise.name: Cable One Arm Twisting Seated Row
aliases: One-arm seated cable row with rotation

reference.title: Cable one arm twisting seated row
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder extension, scapular retraction, elbow flexion, trunk rotation)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you row and turn the chest toward the working side, breathe in as you reach and turn back.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s pull, short squeeze, about 2 s return

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure (RIR 2-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen and lighter than for a two-arm row: the turn must stay smooth and controlled.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a plate; slower turn back

cues.text: Sit tall facing the low pulley, feet braced on the plate, knees soft; hold the handle in the right hand, arm long, right shoulder reaching forward with the chest turned a little to the left; left hand on the hip.
Breathe out; turn the chest back to the right as you row the handle to the side of the stomach, elbow close to the body.
Elbow behind the trunk, shoulder blade drawn back, chest turned slightly right; sit tall.
Breathe in; let the arm reach forward and the right shoulder follow it as the chest turns back to the left, under control.
Brief stretch at full reach without rounding the back, then repeat; switch arms after the set.

mistakes.fix: Lighten the load and turn smoothly with the row.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting from the lower back and hips
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips square on the seat; let the rotation come from the upper back and shoulder blade.
Reach with the shoulder blade and a long spine, not by slumping.
Draw the shoulder blade back and down.

kinematics.norm: Moderate upper-back rotation, hips square on the seat (clinical opinion)
From slightly forward at the reach to upright at the finish, neutral spine (clinical opinion); seated or supported rows kept lumbar loads lower than free bent-over rows (Fenwick 2009)
From nearly straight to about 90-100 degrees (clinical opinion)
Protracted at the reach, retracted at the finish; retraction drives the middle trapezius and rhomboids (Oyama 2010)
Controlled, about 1 s pull and 2 s return (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable one arm twisting seated row, video (movement reference)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the back, shoulder or elbow, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can turn and row smoothly, without jerking the spine.
People with a current back problem should check with a clinician before loaded trunk rotation.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Back discomfort with the turn: do the one-arm row without rotation, chest facing the pulley (clinical opinion).
Shoulder discomfort at the reach: shorten the reach.
regressions: One-arm seated cable row without the turn.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back to the side.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Prime mover: draws the right shoulder blade back; it slides forward with the reach.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps pull the upper arm back.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbow as the handle comes in.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Turn the trunk toward the working side and control the turn back.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Turn the trunk toward the working side and control the turn back.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the spine long and upright.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the spine long and upright.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the pelvis square on the seat while the upper body turns.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder girdle; should not shrug.

guides.label: Handle to the side of the stomach as the chest turns
